subject: Invoice discrepancy: unexpected token surge on Oct billing
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@zebranalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@zebranalytics.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice question — Oct usage spike (attached)

Hi Hannah,

We received the October invoice (attached) and are seeing a ~3.6x increase in token consumption versus September. We did not change client-side batching or prompt templates — the only change was a migration of a small ingestion job to your streaming API on 10/12.

Can you help explain:
- Where the extra tokens were attributed (model, endpoint, or request type)?
- Whether this could be a metering/duplication issue from streaming chunk reassembly?

I've attached our top 100 request ids and a CSV excerpt (oct-token-sample.csv). Please let me know what logs or exports you need. We are reviewing cashflow for November and this variance blocks the team from approving payment in full.

Thanks,
Nina Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Zebra Analytics
Billing: billing@zebranalytics.com
Attachment: oct-invoice-2026-10.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: oct-token-sample.csv (text/csv)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@zebranalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question — Oct usage spike (attached)

Hi Nina,

Thanks for flagging this — sorry for the surprise. I'm looping in Marcus (runtime) and Rafael (billing ops) so we can triage. Quick ask from our side: can you confirm whether the ingestion job that moved to streaming used the streaming endpoint with the "chunked" response flag enabled, or whether it sent explicit chunk-ids in metadata? That helps us narrow whether tokens came from client-side retries.

We will:
- Pull request-level metering for 10/10–10/18 for the request IDs you attached.
- Check for duplicate receipt events (replay/duplicate id handling).
- Reconcile model/variant attribution (some customers saw fallbacks to higher-cost variant during a brief capacity event last month).

I will update you within 48 hours with preliminary findings. If you need an interim statement to unblock payment, Rafael can provide a proforma credit hold note.

Best,
Hannah
Finance & Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Nina Patel <nina.patel@zebranalytics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question — Oct usage spike (attached)

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 11:23 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for flagging this — sorry for the surprise. I'm looping in Marcus (runtime) and Rafael (billing ops) so we can triage.

Hi Nina / team,

We pulled the token-level metering for the request ids you provided and ran a diff against your September patterns. Two notable observations:

1) Reassembly duplication: several streaming sessions show a pattern where the client retried with the same session-id but provided overlapping suffixes (we see the same tokens counted twice after reassembly). This appears in ~1.2% of sampled sessions but those sessions were heavy (long context) which amplifies the token delta.

2) Model fallback event on 2026-10-15 02:07 UTC: your requests hit a temporary capacity fallback and were routed to the compatible-variant v2-large instead of v2-medium for ~13 minutes. v2-large emits ~12% more tokens for certain response-formatting heuristics (we have a ticket on normalizing decode behavior).

We are attaching the sample export as oct-token-sample.csv (subset) and a short log excerpt. Immediate steps we recommend:
- Client: ensure idempotency-key === session-id + incremental-chunk-index, or use the streaming-checkpoint header to avoid reassembly duplicates.
- Server/Platform (us): we will push a conservative metering filter to collapse overlapping reassembly windows for the sampled affected period and evaluate broader retroactive application.

Provisional impact estimate: if we collapse the overlapping reassembly windows for the flagged sessions and apply a model-attribution correction for the 13-minute fallback, Zebra's October bill reduces by ~18.4%. This is preliminary. Rafael, can you propose a provisional credit and an approval path?

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer — Serving Runtime
Attachment: oct-token-sample.csv (text/csv)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@zebranalytics.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 20:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question — Oct usage spike (attached)

Hi Nina — thanks for your patience while we investigated.

Summary of findings (short):
- Root causes: (A) streaming reassembly duplicates for a subset of long sessions; (B) a 13-minute model fallback to v2-large on 2026-10-15 02:07 UTC. Both contributed to the token spike.
- Evidence: token-level export match to your request ids, server routing logs, and the sample CSV we exchanged.

Resolution proposal:
1) Apply an 18.4% pro-rated credit to the Oct invoice to account for collapsed duplicates and model-attribution correction. Credit will be reflected as a separate line item on a corrected invoice (Credit ID: CR-ZEB-20261105).
2) VAT handling: since Zebra is US-based (no EU VAT), we will not apply VAT adjustments. If your billing entity changes region, please notify billing@redwood.com.
3) Production guidance: Marcus's recommendations on idempotency and the streaming-checkpoint header; we will also deploy a server-side conservative filter for the affected window to prevent similar double-counting going forward.

Next steps:
- I will issue the corrected invoice and credit note by EOB Friday (11/6).
- If you accept the credit proposal, please reply with approval and we'll place the original invoice on hold pending the corrected statement.

If you'd like a quick call to walk through the logs and credits, happy to schedule 30 minutes.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192
Attachment: Credit-CR-ZEB-20261105.pdf (application/pdf)
